subject: Bridged installment discount + surge buffer — renewal proposal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Leo Martinez <leo@novaflow.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Bridged installment discount + surge buffer

Hi Leo —

Hope you and the Novaflow team are doing well. As your renewal window approaches (contract ends 2026-09-30), I wanted to share an initial proposal we think balances predictability and flexibility for Novaflow as you scale into H2. Attached is a short SOW and a usage snapshot for Q2.

High level proposal (for 12-month renewal):
- Commit: 1.2M tokens/month baseline (12-month term).
- Bridged installment: 40% of the first-quarter commitment invoiced upfront, followed by equal monthly installments. This lowers OPEX friction for expansion months.
- Installment discount: 6% discount applied to the first installment payment as an adoption stimulus.
- Surge buffer: 25% burst capacity above baseline available at a capped overage rate (20% discount to paygo) for the first 6 months of the term.
- Price hold: we can hold current rates for 90 days post-signature for any committed SKU increase.

Two asks from our side: confirmation of the target baseline (can we lock to 1.2M or would you prefer 1.0M?), and whether procurement will require a PO prior to signature.

If this looks reasonable, we can send a redlined amendment and a DocuSign for signature. Happy to slot a short 20-minute call this week to walk through.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: Novaflow_SOW_v2.pdf, usage_report_Q2.csv

From: Leo Martinez <leo@novaflow.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaflow.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 10:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: Bridged installment discount + surge buffer

Ben — thanks for the proposal and the usage snapshot. A few quick notes from our side after a run-through with engineering and procurement: 

- Baseline: we're leaning toward 1.5M tokens/month for the new term (we saw higher inference volumes in July experiments). Can you reprice for that?
- Price hold: 90 days is helpful, but procurement needs a 6-month price hold at the committed level to coordinate our internal budgets. Is that negotiable?
- Surge capacity: we will likely need the burst buffer to be available immediately for the first 90 days (not staged). We may only pay for actual surge usage but want assurances on availability.
- Early-payment incentive: if you can provide a commercial for a 3% early-payment discount on the first two quarters, procurement may be willing to issue an upfront PO.

Also attach the internal cost model and I'll ask procurement to confirm PO timing. Can you return a single-page term summary we can take to procurement next week?

Cheers,
Leo
Head of Platform | Novaflow
leo@novaflow.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal: Bridged installment discount + surge buffer

Ben / Naomi — quick internal notes after Leo's reply. Strategy suggestion: give a clear dual-path commercial so Novaflow can choose the risk profile they prefer.

Path A (Higher commitment, better economics)
- Commit: 1.5M tokens/mo (12 months)
- Pricing: 8% volume discount vs current list on committed units
- Installment: 50% upfront of Q1 (to ease cash cycle) with 3% early-pay discount on Q1+Q2 if PO is received within 30 days
- Surge: immediate access to 25% burst available for first 180 days at a capped overage price (15% discount to paygo)
- Price hold: 6-month price hold on committed SKUs

Path B (Lower risk, more flexibility)
- Commit: 1.2M tokens/mo (12 months)
- Pricing: 5% volume discount on committed units
- Installment: 40% upfront, no early-pay incentive
- Surge: same burst but subject to capacity gating during peak windows (we'll guarantee availability during agreed maintenance windows)
- Price hold: 90 days

Operational asks: Naomi, can you run the margin impact for Path A vs Path B and confirm whether we can absorb the extended 6-month hold? I attached a draft amendment and a short redline that maps to these two paths (draft_amendment_redlined.docx).

If we land Path A it will be higher ARR and cleaner commit velocity. If Novaflow prefers Path B, we keep optionality while preserving a modest discount. I recommend we present both options in a one-page term sheet for procurement (Leo asked for a single page). I can draft that if you want.

—Marissa
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: draft_amendment_redlined.docx

Leo — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarity on what procurement needs. Per our internal discussion, please find a concise one-page term summary below (I'm pasting here for convenience and attaching the same as a PDF). If this matches, I'll route a redlined amendment and DocuSign link.

One-page term summary (pick A or B):

Path A (Recommended)
- Commit: 1.5M tokens/month; 12-month term (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30)
- Committed discount: 8% off current list pricing on committed units
- Installment: 50% of Q1 committed amount invoiced at signature; remaining installments monthly
- Early-payment incentive: 3% discount applied to Q1+Q2 if PO arrives and payment is processed within 30 days of signature
- Surge buffer: 25% immediate burst capacity for first 180 days; surge billed at capped overage rate (paygo less 15%)
- Price hold: 6 months on committed SKUs after signature

Path B (Optional)
- Commit: 1.2M tokens/month; 12-month term
- Committed discount: 5%
- Installment: 40% upfront; no early-pay discount
- Surge buffer: 25% burst but subject to capacity gating (guaranteed during maintenance windows)
- Price hold: 90 days

Next steps:
1) Confirm which path Novaflow prefers (A or B) and whether procurement can issue a PO (we can accept PO prior to DocuSign to unblock billing).
2) If OK, we will send a redlined amendment and a DocuSign (link: https://redwood.docusign.com/DEAL-7832).
3) Marissa will follow with the redline and Naomi will confirm margin impact internally.

If you want to jump on a 20-min call to finalize language for procurement, I'm available tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks and talk soon —
Ben Carter
